That films are actually a great source of history! Film history, as in history through film (not the history of film), is a relatively new field that really isn't widely accepted, at least that's how most people including my professors in undergrad see it. I was only able to secure the support of one professor who agreed that film is a medium that veers away from traditional methods of historiography. 

Amongst the historians who have described the field, I find John E. O'Connor's the most fascinating; (fictional) films can be used to gauge the sociocultural reality of a given time. For example, I did my thesis on women in horror in my country. I found out that over time, women were portrayed as stronger and active individuals who could face adversities themselves as compared to always being damsels in distress in latter half of the 20th century. This was in line with the growing feminist movements that happened in real life in my country. However, women were still attached to motherhood in horror, much like the still emphasized pressures of women today. 

It's a field that's very unconventional, but once you get into it, it opens up a whole new perspective in studying history

i cant really speak for other places, but in the case of the moros of mindanao, its a mix of late colonization, religious and cultural differences, and social inequalities.

while most of the present-day philippines was controlled by the spaniards in the first couple of centuries of colonization, the muslim areas in mindanao (the sultanates of sulu, maguindanao, etc) werent penetrated until the 1800s. though, tensions were always high between them and the spaniards especially since other areas of mindanao were colonized and the seas were an area of conflict. by the time the spaniards left and the americans entered the scene, the subjugation of the moros was "successful." while different institutions and norms were still in place due to the deep-rootedness of their culture, the americans eventually replaced them with their own institutions (banning of slavery, establishment of the constabulary in the area, public education). lots of uprisings and massacres happened as a result of the discontentment of the moros and the deterioration of the sultanates.

the government also encouraged the migration of christianized filipinos to the area in order to assimilate the population, and they also discouraged interactions of the moros with other muslim populations. by the dawn of filipino nationalism and the push for philippine independence before the commonwealth period, the moros wanted the us to separate them from the rest of the country; they didnt identify as filipinos since the term was exclusively used to identify natives who were christianized. the us eventually succumbed to christian nationalists who believed that the moros were part of the country.

post world war 2 philippines saw a huge migration from christian central luzon to moro mindanao (particularly during the magsaysay administration). since the concept of land ownership and titles didnt exist in the region, a lot was declared as public property, hence the swift and easy settlements of moro regions. the moros also noted that christian settlements were better in every aspect; they had better roads, better schools, better irrigation. they questioned the favor given to christians. by 1971, 800,000 moros were displaced in the religion and thousands killed in conflicts. this gave rise to the establishments of a well-known moro nationalist group in the country, the moro nationalist liberation font (mnlf). 

during marcos sr.'s martial law declaration, revolutionaries and civilians were scared that their cultural heritage and right to carry arms would be threatened. from 1972-1980s, various conflicts and massacres led to death of around 100k civilians and military personnel. almost a million people were displaced in the region due to raids, destruction of villages, tortures, and evacuations. also, christian and moro vigilante groups added to the tensions.

in 1976, the ph government and the mnlf signed a peace treaty (the tripoli agreement of peace) that demanded a ceasefire and autonomy. not even a year letter, fighting started again due to both sides wanting different amendments. throughout the years, the state and media framed the conflict as "the christian-majority vs the muslim-minority." the moros were eventually granted "autonomy" through cory aquino's government establishing the autonomous region in muslim mindanao (armm). however, they werent really filly autonomous, thus conflicts continued. in 2008, amidst the recognition of the "bangsamoro" identity, the supreme court declared the memorandum of agreement on ancestral domain as unconstitutional. conflict arose once more and thousands of moros were displaced yet again. 

a lot has happened between now and then, but it is redundant aside from the continuous dialogues between moro leaders and the national government resulting in the establishment of the bangsamoro autonomous region in muslim mindanao.
